subject: botany
question_text: Discuss the various types of pollen tube entry into ovary with the help of diagrams.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section (book p.20, LAQ 4). Botany holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The book prints the same three-panel entry figure twice (in LAQ 2 and LAQ 4); this card draws it once, as three simplified ovules with the route labelled on each. In LAQ 2 the book defines mesogamy as entry 'through integument (or) funiculus'; here and in the standard definition it is through the integuments.

page_header: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants · 8 marks

steps.label: The three methods
lines: After pollen germination the pollen tube
passes through the style and enters the
ovary.
It then enters the ovule by any one of three
methods:
A) Porogamy B) Chalazogamy C) Mesogamy
steps.why: The classification is by doorway into the ovule — before describing each route, show the journey up to the ovary and name all three methods, which is the listing mark.
common_mistakes: Naming only porogamy. The question says 'various types' — all three must appear.
Writing that the tube enters the ovary three ways. The three ways are into the OVULE; the tube reaches the ovary through the style in every case.
steps.memory_tip: One road to the ovary, three doors into the ovule: pore, base, wall.
steps.margin_note: The A/B/C list up front earns the naming mark before any description.

steps.label: Porogamy
lines: Porogamy: the pollen tube enters the ovule
through the micropyle.
This is the most common method.
Example: Ottelia.
steps.why: The micropyle is the ovule's natural pore, already pointing at the egg apparatus — which is why this route is the usual one in flowering plants.
common_mistakes: Pairing porogamy with Casuarina — Casuarina is the chalazogamy example; Ottelia goes here.
Omitting 'most common' — it is the extra fact this route carries.
steps.memory_tip: PORO = pore. The micropyle IS the pore, so porogamy is entry through the micropyle.
steps.margin_note: Route + 'most common' + example: three short lines.

steps.label: Chalazogamy
lines: Chalazogamy: the pollen tube enters the ovule
through the chalaza, the basal part opposite
the micropyle.
Example: Casuarina.
steps.why: The chalaza is the end where the integuments arise, opposite the micropyle — entry there means the tube comes in from the far end, as in Casuarina.
common_mistakes: Placing the chalaza next to the micropyle. They are OPPOSITE ends of the ovule.
steps.memory_tip: The name contains the door: CHALAZ-ogamy = through the CHALAZA. Casuarina is its plant.
steps.margin_note: Route + the 'opposite end' fact + example — one compact point.

steps.label: Mesogamy
lines: Mesogamy: the pollen tube enters the ovule
through the integuments, between the two
ends.
Example: Cucurbita.
steps.why: Meso means middle: the tube pierces the side coverings of the ovule rather than using either end — the Cucurbita route.
common_mistakes: Confusing mesogamy with porogamy. Micropyle = porogamy; the side integuments = mesogamy.
Missing the example. Cucurbita (gourd family) is the stated one.
steps.memory_tip: MESO = middle. Not the pore, not the base — through the wall in the middle.
steps.margin_note: The book's LAQ 2 adds 'or funiculus' for this route; integuments is the standard answer.

steps.label: Diagrams — the three entry routes
steps.why: The question says 'with the help of diagrams', so the three panels carry real marks: the same ovule drawn three times with the tube coming through the micropyle, the chalaza, and the integuments.
common_mistakes: Drawing three different ovules. Keep the ovule identical so only the tube's route changes.
Sending the chalazogamy tube through the top but stopping it outside — every tube must reach the embryo sac.
Forgetting to label the route on each panel.
steps.memory_tip: One ovule, photocopied three times; only the tube moves: bottom door, top door, side wall.
steps.margin_note: Three small panels beat one large drawing — label the route under each.

steps.label: Common end point

lines.text: All three routes end at a synergid

lines: Whatever the entry route, the pollen tube
finally enters a synergid through the
filiform apparatus and releases the two male
gametes there.
steps.why: The unifying fact closes the discussion: the routes differ only in the doorway — the destination (a synergid, via the filiform apparatus) is the same in all three.
common_mistakes: Ending the answer at the three routes without the common destination — the book itself states this line.
Writing that the tube enters the egg. It enters a synergid; the gametes then reach the egg and the central cell.
steps.memory_tip: Three doors, one room: every tube finishes inside a synergid.
steps.margin_note: The boxed unifying line is the examiner's finish — do not stop at the third route.

insider_note: The plural 'diagrams' in the question is literal — one drawing of porogamy alone forfeits the diagram marks; three small labelled panels is what full marks looks like.
